To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the differential contributions of bilateral SMAS to ECN during motor execution and motor imagination are modulated by the task condition, and the left SMA is involved in the right hand motor execution.

bilateral supplementary motor area plays a different role during motor execution and motor imagination and the hemispheric recruitment of the left SMA is observed during the execution of left hand tasks.

the task conditions induced the differential contributions of bilateral supplementary motor area to the effective connectivity networks, and the hemiparetic pattern of effective connectivity networks was found during motor imagery.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the hemispherical asymmetry of SMA contributions during lateralized tasks.
the differential contribution of the bilateral SMAs in the effective connectivity network during motor tasks.
the differential contributions of bilateral SM As in the effective connectivity during unimanual lateralized motor tasks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the differential contribution of left and right SMAs to the motor network was induced by task condition.
the hemispherally asymmetric roles of bilateral SMAS were induced by the task conditions, especially the task input of the motor execution/imagary, in the ECN among regions.

the differential contributions of bilateral SMAS during unimanual execution/imagery and the hemispheric asymmetrical patterns of ECN were induced by task condition, which may be related to the hemispherized recruitment of SMA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hemispherized roles of bilateral SMA in the ECN are task-dependent, and that the hemispheric asymmetries of the ECN are not only induced by task input, but also by the intrinsic coupling.
the hemispherally asymmetrical roles of bilateral SMA were induced by different task conditions.
, in the ECN, the bilateral SMA played different roles in different task conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hemispherally asymmetric roles of bilateral SMAS on the ECN are dependent on the task conditions, and the task input modulated the ECN in the motor execution and imagery.
the task input modulated the ECNs among regions involved during the motor execution/imaginary.
the hemispherical special roles of bilateral SMA in the ECN are not fixed but can be dynamically altered according to task demands.
